sanskrit: yat pṛthivyāṃ puṇyatamaṃ vidyāsthānaṃ tadāvaset yateta tasmin prāmāṇyaṃ gantuṃ yaśasi cottame
english: Let him dwell in whatever seat of learning is most holy upon the earth, and there strive to attain authority and the highest renown.

sanskrit: tapasā vā sumahatā vidyānāṃ pāraṇena vā ijyayā vā pradānair vā viprāṇāṃ vardhate yaśaḥ
english: By mighty austerity, by mastering the whole range of the sciences, by sacrifice, or by gifts, the renown of the learned brāhmaṇa grows.

sanskrit: yāvad asya bhavaty asmiṃl loke kīrtir yaśaskarī tāvat puṇyakṛtāṃl lokān anantān puruṣo 'śnute
english: For as long as his glory-bringing fame endures in this world, so long does a man enjoy the endless realms won by the doers of holy deeds.

sanskrit: adhyāpayed adhīyīta yājayeta yajeta ca na vṛthā pratigṛhṇīyān na ca dadyāt kathaṃ cana
english: Let him teach and let him study, let him officiate at sacrifices and offer his own; but let him never accept a gift without cause, nor ever give one so.

sanskrit: yājyataḥ śiṣyato vāpi kanyayā vā dhanaṃ mahat yady āgacched yajed dadyān naiko 'śnīyāt kathaṃ cana
english: If great wealth should come to him from one for whom he sacrifices, or from a pupil, or by a bride's dowry, let him sacrifice and give it away; let him never enjoy it alone.

sanskrit: gṛham āvasato hy asya nānyat tīrthaṃ pratigrahāt devarṣipitṛgurvarthaṃ vṛddhāturabubhukṣatām
english: For the householder there is no fit occasion for accepting gifts save this: for the sake of the gods, the seers, the ancestors, and the teacher, and for the aged, the sick, and the hungry.

sanskrit: antarhitābhitaptānāṃ yathāśakti bubhūṣatām dravyāṇām atiśaktyāpi deyam eṣāṃ kṛtād api
english: To those who are ruined and stricken yet wish, as best they can, to lift themselves up, one should give of one's goods even beyond one's power, even past what duty requires.

sanskrit: arhatām anurūpāṇāṃ nādeyaṃ hy asti kiṃ cana uccaiḥśravasam apy aśvaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ satāṃ viduḥ
english: To the worthy and the fitting there is nothing that may not be given; the good hold that even a steed like Uccaiḥśravas should be bestowed upon them.

sanskrit: anunīya tathā kāvyaḥ satyasaṃdho mahāvrataḥ svaiḥ prāṇair brāhmaṇaprāṇān paritrāya divaṃ gataḥ
english: So it was that Kāvya, true to his word and bound by mighty vows, won over and saved the lives of brāhmaṇas with his own life, and went to heaven.

sanskrit: rantidevaś ca sāṃkṛtyo vasiṣṭhāya mahātmane apaḥ pradāya śītoṣṇā nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate
english: And Rantideva, son of Saṃkṛti, having given cool and warm waters to the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, is honored upon the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: ātreyaś candradamayor arhator vividhaṃ dhanam dattvā lokān yayau dhīmān anantān sa mahīpatiḥ
english: The wise king of Atri's line, having given manifold wealth to the worthy Candra and Dama, departed to the endless worlds.

sanskrit: śibirauśīnaro 'ṅgāni sutaṃ ca priyam aurasam brāhmaṇārtham upākṛtya nākapṛṣṭham ito gataḥ
english: Śibi, son of Uśīnara, having offered up his own limbs and his dear-born son for a brāhmaṇa's sake, passed from here to the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: pratardanaḥ kāśipatiḥ pradāya nayane svake brāhmaṇāyātulāṃ kīrtim iha cāmutra cāśnute
english: Pratardana, lord of Kāśi, having given his own eyes to a brāhmaṇa, enjoys matchless fame both in this world and in the next.

sanskrit: divyaṃ mṛṣṭaśalākaṃ tu sauvarṇaṃ paramarddhimat chatraṃ devāvṛdho dattvā sarāṣṭro 'bhyapatad divam
english: Devāvṛdha, having given a divine parasol of gold with polished ribs and of supreme splendor, ascended to heaven together with his realm.

sanskrit: sāṃkṛtiś ca tathātreyaḥ śiṣyebhyo brahma nirguṇam upadiśya mahātejā gato lokān anuttamān
english: And Sāṃkṛti of Atri's line, mighty in splendor, having taught his pupils the brahman that is beyond all qualities, went to the unsurpassed worlds.

sanskrit: ambarīṣo gavāṃ dattvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pratāpavān arbudāni daśaikaṃ ca sarāṣṭro 'bhyapatad divam
english: The mighty Ambarīṣa, having given eleven hundred million cows to brāhmaṇas, ascended to heaven together with his realm.

sanskrit: sāvitrī kuṇḍale divye śarīraṃ janamejayaḥ brāhmaṇārthe parityajya jagmatur lokam uttamam
english: Sāvitrī, giving up her two divine earrings, and Janamejaya, giving up his body, both for a brāhmaṇa's sake, went to the highest world.

sanskrit: sarvaratnaṃ vṛṣādarbho yuvanāśvaḥ priyāḥ striyaḥ ramyam āvasathaṃ caiva dattvāmuṃ lokam āsthitaḥ
english: Vṛṣādarbha and Yuvanāśva, having given away all their jewels, their beloved women, and their delightful dwelling, attained that other world.

sanskrit: nimī rāṣṭraṃ ca vaideho jāmadagnyo vasuṃdharām brāhmaṇebhyo dadau cāpi gayaś corvīṃ sapattanām
english: Nimi of Videha gave his kingdom, the son of Jamadagni gave the whole earth, and Gaya too gave the broad earth with its cities, all to brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: avarṣati ca parjanye sarvabhūtāni cāsakṛt vasiṣṭho jīvayām āsa prajāpatir iva prajāḥ
english: And when the rain-cloud withheld its rain, again and again Vasiṣṭha kept all creatures alive, as Prajāpati keeps his offspring.

sanskrit: karaṃdhamasya putras tu marutto nṛpatis tathā kanyām aṅgirase dattvā divam āśu jagāma ha
english: And King Marutta, son of Karaṃdhama, having given his daughter to Aṅgiras, swiftly went to heaven.

sanskrit: brahmadattaś ca pāñcālyo rājā buddhimatāṃ varaḥ nidhiṃ śaṅkhaṃ dvijāgryebhyo dattvā lokān avāptavān
english: And Brahmadatta of Pāñcāla, that king foremost among the wise, having given the treasure-conch to the chief of the twice-born, won the higher worlds.

sanskrit: rājā mitrasahaś cāpi vasiṣṭhāya mahātmane madayantīṃ priyāṃ dattvā tayā saha divaṃ gataḥ
english: And King Mitrasaha too, having given his beloved Madayantī to the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, went to heaven together with her.

sanskrit: sahasrajic ca rājarṣiḥ prāṇān iṣṭān mahāyaśāḥ brāhmaṇārthe parityajya gato lokān anuttamān
english: And the royal seer Sahasrajit of great fame, having given up his cherished life for a brāhmaṇa's sake, went to the unsurpassed worlds.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaiś ca saṃpūrṇaṃ dattvā veśma hiraṇmayam mudgalāya gataḥ svargaṃ śatadyumno mahīpatiḥ
english: And King Śatadyumna, having given to Mudgala a golden mansion filled with all that heart could wish, went to heaven.

sanskrit: nāmnā ca dyutimān nāma śālvarājaḥ pratāpavān dattvā rājyam ṛcīkāya gato lokān anuttamān
english: And the mighty king of the Śālvas, Dyutimān by name, having given his kingdom to Ṛcīka, went to the unsurpassed worlds.

sanskrit: madirāśvaś ca rājarṣir dattvā kanyāṃ sumadhyamām hiraṇyahastāya gato lokān devair abhiṣṭutān
english: And the royal seer Madirāśva, having given his fair-waisted daughter to Hiraṇyahasta, went to the worlds extolled by the gods.

sanskrit: lomapādaś ca rājarṣiḥ śāntāṃ dattvā sutāṃ prabhuḥ ṛśyaśṛṅgāya vipulaiḥ sarvakāmair ayujyata
english: And the royal seer Lomapāda, the lord, having given his daughter Śāntā to Ṛśyaśṛṅga, was joined with all his abundant desires fulfilled.

sanskrit: dattvā śatasahasraṃ tu gavāṃ rājā prasenajit savatsānāṃ mahātejā gato lokān anuttamān
english: And King Prasenajit of great splendor, having given a hundred thousand cows together with their calves, went to the unsurpassed worlds.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo dānena tapasā ca ha mahātmāno gatāḥ svargaṃ śiṣṭātmāno jitendriyāḥ
english: These and many others, great-souled, refined of spirit and masters of their senses, went to heaven by giving and by austerity.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ pratiṣṭhitā kīrtir yāvat sthāsyati medinī dānayajñaprajāsargair ete hi divam āpnuvan
english: Their fame stands firm for as long as the earth shall endure; by gifts, by sacrifices, and by the begetting of offspring, these men attained heaven.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca trayīvidyām avekṣeta vedeṣūktām athāṅgataḥ ṛksāmavarṇākṣarato yajuṣo 'tharvaṇas tathā
english: Vyāsa said: Let him study the threefold knowledge as set forth in the Vedas, and then through its ancillary sciences — through the words and syllables of the Ṛk and the Sāman, and likewise of the Yajus and the Atharvan.

sanskrit: vedavādeṣu kuśalā hy adhyātmakuśalāś ca ye sattvavanto mahābhāgāḥ paśyanti prabhavāpyayau
english: For those who are skilled in the doctrines of the Veda and skilled in the knowledge of the self, men of purity and great fortune, behold the arising and the passing away of things.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmeṇa varteta kriyāḥ śiṣṭavad ācaret asaṃrodhena bhūtānāṃ vṛttiṃ lipseta vai dvijaḥ
english: Thus let him conduct himself by dharma and perform his rites as the cultured do; without injury to living beings let the twice-born seek his livelihood.

sanskrit: sadbhya āgatavijñānaḥ śiṣṭaḥ śāstravicakṣaṇaḥ svadharmeṇa kriyā loke kurvāṇaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: Having received understanding from the good, cultured and learned in the scriptures, performing his rites in the world by his own dharma, true to his pledged word —

sanskrit: tiṣṭhaty eteṣu gṛhavān ṣaṭsu karmasu sa dvijaḥ pañcabhiḥ satataṃ yajñaiḥ śraddadhāno yajeta ca
english: Such a twice-born householder abides in these six observances; and full of faith let him ever worship with the five sacrifices.

sanskrit: dhṛtimān apramattaś ca dānto dharmavid ātmavān vītaharṣabhayakrodho brāhmaṇo nāvasīdati
english: Steadfast and vigilant, self-restrained, knowing dharma, master of himself, free of elation, fear, and wrath — such a brāhmaṇa does not sink.

sanskrit: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñas tapo hrīr ārjavaṃ damaḥ etair vardhayate tejaḥ pāpmānaṃ cāpakarṣati
english: Giving, study, sacrifice, austerity, modesty, uprightness, and self-control — by these he increases his spiritual fire and casts off all evil.

sanskrit: dhūtapāpmā tu medhāvī laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ kāmakrodhau vaśe kṛtvā ninīṣed brahmaṇaḥ padam
english: Then, his sins shaken off, wise, of light diet, his senses conquered, having brought desire and wrath under his sway, let him strive toward the abode of brahman.

sanskrit: agnīṃś ca brāhmaṇāṃś cārced devatāḥ praṇameta ca varjayed ruṣatīṃ vācaṃ hiṃsāṃ cādharmasaṃhitām
english: Let him honor the sacred fires and the brāhmaṇas and bow before the gods; let him shun harsh speech and all violence bound up with unrighteousness.

sanskrit: eṣā pūrvatarā vṛttir brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate jñānāgamena karmāṇi kurvan karmasu sidhyati
english: This is ordained as the more ancient way of life for the brāhmaṇa; performing his works with the acquisition of knowledge, he attains perfection in his works.

sanskrit: pañcendriyajalāṃ ghorāṃ lobhakūlāṃ sudustarām manyupaṅkām anādhṛṣyāṃ nadīṃ tarati buddhimān
english: The wise man crosses that dreadful river, hard to ford and unassailable, whose waters are the five senses, whose banks are greed, and whose mire is wrath.

sanskrit: kāmamanyūddhataṃ yat syān nityam atyantamohitam mahatā vidhidṛṣṭena balenāpratighātinā svabhāvasrotasā vṛttam uhyate satataṃ jagat
english: This world, ever risen up by desire and wrath, ever utterly deluded, is borne along without ceasing upon the current of its own nature, by a mighty force seen in the ordinance of things, a force that none can resist.

sanskrit: kālodakena mahatā varṣāvartena saṃtatam māsormiṇartuvegena pakṣolapatṛṇena ca
english: With the great waters that are time, in the unbroken whirl of the year's rains, with the months for waves and the seasons for current, with the fortnights for the grass that floats upon it —

sanskrit: nimeṣonmeṣaphenena ahorātrajavena ca kāmagrāheṇa ghoreṇa vedayajñaplavena ca
english: with the closing and opening of an eye for its foam, with the rush of day and night for its swiftness, with the dread crocodile that is desire, and with the raft that is the Veda and sacrifice —

sanskrit: dharmadvīpena bhūtānāṃ cārthakāmaraveṇa ca ṛtasopānatīreṇa vihiṃsātaruvāhinā
english: with dharma for the island of living beings, with the roar of wealth and desire, with the shore whose stairway is righteousness, bearing along the trees that are acts of violence —

sanskrit: yugahradaughamadhyena brahmaprāyabhavena ca dhātrā sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kṛṣyante yamasādanam
english: and through whose midst flows the flood of the ages' deep pools, with brahman for its origin and its end — into this river the Ordainer has cast all creatures, and they are dragged down to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: etat prajñāmayair dhīrā nistaranti manīṣiṇaḥ plavair aplavavanto hi kiṃ kariṣyanty acetasaḥ
english: This the steadfast and the wise cross over by rafts fashioned of insight; but the unthinking, who have no raft, what shall they do?

sanskrit: upapannaṃ hi yat prājño nistaren netaro janaḥ dūrato guṇadoṣau hi prājñaḥ sarvatra paśyati
english: For it is fitting that the wise man should cross over, and not the common run of folk; for the wise man, in all things, sees merit and fault from afar.

sanskrit: saṃśayātmā sa kāmātmā calacitto 'lpacetanaḥ aprājño na taraty eva yo hy āste na sa gacchati
english: The man whose soul is full of doubt and desire, of wavering mind and feeble understanding, the unwise — he cannot cross over at all; for he who sits idle does not move forward.

sanskrit: aplavo hi mahādoṣam uhyamāno 'dhigacchati kāmagrāhagṛhītasya jñānam apy asya na plavaḥ
english: For the man without a raft, swept along, meets with great disaster; and for one seized by the crocodile of desire, even his knowledge is no raft.

sanskrit: tasmād unmajjanasyārthe prayateta vicakṣaṇaḥ etad unmajjanaṃ tasya yad ayaṃ brāhmaṇo bhavet
english: Therefore let the discerning man strive for the sake of rising up out of the flood; and this is his rising up — that he becomes a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tryavadāte kule jātas trisaṃdehas trikarmakṛt tasmād unmajjanas tiṣṭhen nistaret prajñayā yathā
english: Born in a family pure through three generations, of threefold lineage, doer of the three rites — let him therefore stand ready to rise up, that he may cross over by his insight.

sanskrit: saṃskṛtasya hi dāntasya niyatasya kṛtātmanaḥ prājñasyānantarā siddhir iha loke paratra ca
english: For the man who is refined, self-restrained, disciplined, perfected in soul, and wise, perfection comes without delay, both in this world and the next.

sanskrit: vartate teṣu gṛhavān akrudhyann anasūyakaḥ pañcabhiḥ satataṃ yajñair vighasāśī yajeta ca
english: The householder abides in these observances, free of anger and free of envy; let him ever worship with the five sacrifices and eat what remains after the offering.

sanskrit: satāṃ vṛttena varteta kriyāḥ śiṣṭavad ācaret asaṃrodhena dharmasya vṛttiṃ lipsed agarhitām
english: Let him conduct himself by the practice of the good and perform his rites as the cultured do; without violating dharma, let him seek a blameless livelihood.

sanskrit: śrutivijñānatattvajñaḥ śiṣṭācāro vicakṣaṇaḥ svadharmeṇa kriyāvāṃś ca karmaṇā so 'py asaṃkaraḥ
english: Knowing the truth through scripture and discernment, of cultured conduct, discerning, active in his own dharma — by his works he too remains undefiled.

sanskrit: kriyāvāñ śraddadhānaś ca dātā prājño 'nasūyakaḥ dharmādharmaviśeṣajñaḥ sarvaṃ tarati dustaram
english: Active in rites, full of faith, generous, wise, free of envy, knowing well the difference between right and wrong — he crosses over all that is hard to cross.

sanskrit: dhṛtimān apramattaś ca dānto dharmavid ātmavān vītaharṣabhayakrodho brāhmaṇo nāvasīdati
english: Steadfast and vigilant, self-restrained, knowing dharma, master of himself, free of elation, fear, and wrath — such a brāhmaṇa does not sink.

sanskrit: eṣā pūrvatarā vṛttir brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate jñānavittvena karmāṇi kurvan sarvatra sidhyati
english: This is ordained as the more ancient way of life for the brāhmaṇa; performing his works through the possession of knowledge, he attains perfection everywhere.

sanskrit: adharmaṃ dharmakāmo hi karotīhāvicakṣaṇaḥ dharmaṃ cādharmasaṃkāśaṃ śocann iva karoti saḥ
english: For here the undiscerning man, though he desires dharma, does unrighteousness; and dharma that looks like unrighteousness he performs as if in sorrow.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ karomīti karoty adharmam; adharmakāmaś ca karoti dharmam ubhe bālaḥ karmaṇī na prajānan; sa jāyate mriyate cāpi dehī
english: Thinking 'I do dharma,' he does unrighteousness; and desiring unrighteousness, he sometimes does dharma. The fool, not understanding either of these two deeds — that embodied one is born and dies again and again.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca atha ced rocayed etad druhyeta manasā tathā unmajjaṃś ca nimajjaṃś ca jñānavān plavavān bhavet
english: Vyāsa said: But if a man should set his heart upon this, and bend his mind toward it with resolve, then, now rising and now sinking, the man of knowledge becomes one possessed of a raft.

sanskrit: prajñayā nirmitair dhīrās tārayanty abudhān plavaiḥ nābudhās tārayanty anyān ātmānaṃ vā kathaṃ cana
english: By rafts fashioned of insight the steadfast carry the ignorant across; but the ignorant can in no way carry others across, nor even themselves.

sanskrit: chinnadoṣo munir yogān yukto yuñjīta dvādaśa daśakarmasukhān arthān upāyāpāyanirbhayaḥ
english: With his faults cut away, the sage, intent and disciplined, should practice the twelvefold yoga, free of fear in approaching or withdrawing, his ends the joys that flow from the ten observances.

sanskrit: cakṣur ācāravit prājño manasā darśanena ca yacched vāṅmanasī buddhyā ya icchej jñānam uttamam jñānena yacched ātmānaṃ ya icchec chāntim ātmanaḥ
english: He who would attain the highest knowledge, wise and skilled in conduct, should restrain his sight by the mind and by insight, and restrain speech and mind by the intellect; and he who would attain the soul's peace should restrain the self by knowledge.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ ced anudraṣṭā puruṣo 'pi sudāruṇaḥ yadi vā sarvavedajño yadi vāpy anṛco 'japaḥ
english: If a man becomes a constant beholder of these, though he be most fierce of nature, or though he know all the Vedas, or though he know neither hymn nor muttered prayer —

sanskrit: yadi vā dhārmiko yajvā yadi vā pāpakṛttamaḥ yadi vā puruṣavyāghro yadi vā klaibyadhāritā
english: whether he be righteous and a sacrificer, or the greatest of evildoers, whether he be a tiger among men, or one beset by weakness —

sanskrit: taraty eva mahādurgaṃ jarāmaraṇasāgaram evaṃ hy etena yogena yuñjāno 'py ekam antataḥ api jijñāsamāno hi śabdabrahmātivartate
english: he crosses indeed that great stronghold, the ocean of old age and death; for one who is yoked by this discipline, even practicing but one of these in the end, even merely seeking to know, passes beyond the brahman that is sound.

sanskrit: dharmopastho hrīvarūtha upāyāpāyakūbaraḥ apānākṣaḥ prāṇayugaḥ prajñāyur jīvabandhanaḥ
english: Its seat is dharma, its guard-rail modesty, its pole the approaching and the withdrawing; the down-breath is its axle, the breaths its yoke, insight its span of life, and the living being its tether —

sanskrit: cetanābandhuraś cārur ācāragrahanemivān darśanasparśanavaho ghrāṇaśravaṇavāhanaḥ
english: made fair by consciousness and lovely, its felly the holding fast to right conduct, drawn forward by sight and touch, borne along by smell and hearing —

sanskrit: prajñānābhiḥ sarvatantrapratodo jñānasārathiḥ kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhito dhīraḥ śraddhādamapuraḥsaraḥ
english: its nave wisdom, its goad the mastery of all the doctrines, knowledge its charioteer, ridden over by the Knower of the Field, steadfast, with faith and self-restraint going on before it —

sanskrit: tyāgavartmānugaḥ kṣemyaḥ śaucago dhyānagocaraḥ jīvayukto ratho divyo brahmaloke virājate
english: following the road of renunciation, bringing security, moving in purity, ranging in the field of meditation: this divine chariot, yoked with the living self, shines forth in the world of brahman.

sanskrit: atha saṃtvaramāṇasya ratham etaṃ yuyukṣataḥ akṣaraṃ gantumanaso vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi śīghragam
english: Now to one who, hastening, would yoke this chariot, whose mind is set on reaching the Imperishable, I shall declare the swift-bearing rule.

sanskrit: sapta yo dhāraṇāḥ kṛtsnā vāgyataḥ pratipadyate pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvataś cānyā yāvatyas tāḥ pradhāraṇāḥ
english: He who, restrained in speech, masters in full the seven fixations of the mind, and likewise the others, behind and to the side, however many those further holdings are —

sanskrit: kramaśaḥ pārthivaṃ yac ca vāyavyaṃ khaṃ tathā payaḥ jyotiṣo yat tad aiśvaryam ahaṃkārasya buddhitaḥ
english: in due order the lordship over earth, over the windy element, over space and over water, and that which belongs to light, the lordship over the I-principle that springs from the intellect —

sanskrit: avyaktasya tathaiśvaryaṃ kramaśaḥ pratipadyate vikramāś cāpi yasyaite tathā yuṅkte sa yogataḥ
english: and so too the lordship over the Unmanifest he attains in due order; and he in whom these powers are present yokes himself thus by yoga.

sanskrit: athāsya yogayuktasya siddhim ātmani paśyataḥ nirmathyamānaḥ sūkṣmatvād rūpāṇīmāni darśayet
english: Then, when he is yoked in yoga and beholds the perfection within himself, the self, being churned forth, by reason of its subtlety reveals these forms.

sanskrit: śaiśiras tu yathā dhūmaḥ sūkṣmaḥ saṃśrayate nabhaḥ tathā dehād vimuktasya pūrvarūpaṃ bhavaty uta
english: As the fine smoke of winter clings to the sky, so does the first appearance arise for one who is freed from the body.

sanskrit: atha dhūmasya virame dvitīyaṃ rūpadarśanam jalarūpam ivākāśe tatraivātmani paśyati
english: Then, when the smoke has ceased, comes the second vision of form: he beholds, there in his very self, something like the form of water in the sky.
